text: ← RETURN TO SELECTED WORK CASE STUDY 06 MOBILE UI/UX DESIGN MENTAL WELLNESS FIGMA PROTOTYPE Vellum — Mindful Mobile UX/UI & Ambient Reflection Concept A calm, low-effort mobile journaling concept designed in Figma: no push nagging, no streak counters, and short, gentle reflection prompts instead. View Figma Community File ↗ Launch Interactive Prototype ↗ PLATFORM Figma Interactive Prototype · iOS Guidelines DISCIPLINE Mobile UI/UX & Interaction Design ROLE Product Architect & Interaction Lead STACK Figma · Auto Layout · ProtoPie ● THE DESIGN CHALLENGE My design concern is game-style mechanics in wellness apps: daily push reminders, streak counters and badges. My assumption, which the prototype is built to test, is that for people who are already stressed, missing one day can feel like failing, and that this makes them quit. ● THE ARCHITECTURE SOLUTION Designed a calm journaling companion in Figma: a one-swipe mood check-in, guided breathing, and free writing, with no streaks, no red badges, and a muted palette that is easy on the eyes at night. 0 Streaks NO STREAK COUNTERS OR RED BADGES Protopie Motion PROTOPIE KINETIC MOTION PHYSICS Auto Layout 5 SCALABLE COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE 3 Flows CHECK-IN, BREATHING & FREE WRITING VELLUM // CALM JOURNALING FLOWS ● FIGMA PROTOTYPE # Vellum interaction principles, as designed (a Figma + Protopie prototype) [INPUT] Single-thumb swipe to pick a mood [INTERACTIONS] Three modes to choose from: ├─ Mood check-in (no typing) ├─ Guided breathing (visual pacing) └─ Free writing on a plain page [HEURISTICS] No streak counters · no red badges [PROTOTYPE] Figma + Protopie, Published to the Figma Community TABLE OF CONTENTS 01. Overview & The Problem 02. Design Assumptions 03. Structural Architecture 04. Visual & Interaction Craft 05. Key Outcomes & Takeaways // 01 · CONTEXT & PROBLEM The Paradox of Gamified Wellness The design concern behind Vellum is game-style mechanics in wellness and journaling apps: daily push notifications, streak counters, badge unlocks and busy dashboards. My assumption is that for someone already anxious or burnt out, these can turn a missed day into pressure and shame. “How might we design a mental wellness companion that feels like opening a physical notebook on a quiet morning—calm, non-judgmental, and emotionally safe?” Vellum was conceived to test a contrary hypothesis: by removing gamified streaks and replacing them with ambient breathing exercises, open-ended micro-journaling, and sensory micro-interactions, daily reflection becomes an intrinsically rewarding refuge rather than another item on a to-do list. // 02 · DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS Addressing Cognitive Friction in Journaling I did not run user interviews for Vellum. The design starts from three friction points I took from reviewing common journaling apps; they are assumptions the prototype is built to test, not research findings: 1. The “Blank Page” Paralysis An empty text area asks people to decide what to write before they have started, which makes it easy to close the app instead. 2. Streak Guilt & Burnout A streak counter turns one missed day into a visible failure, which can push people to quit rather than come back. 3. Visual Over-stimulation Bright gradients and saturated colours are harsh on the eyes late at night, when a reflection app is likely to be opened. // 03 · WIREFRAMING & PROGRESSION From Low-Fidelity Logic to Refined Polarity Each core flow was mapped in wireframe form to test hierarchy before introducing typography, tactile shadows, and color temperature. Fig 1.1 — Low-Fidelity Onboarding Wireframe Fig 1.2 — High-Fidelity Onboarding Flow Fig 2.1 — Mood Check-in Wireframe Fig 2.2 — Final Mood Check-in Interface Fig 3.1 — Breathing Rhythm Wireframe Fig 3.2 — Ambient Guided Breathing Screen Fig 3.3 — Recommendation Engine Wireframe Fig 3.4 — Personalized Habit Recommendations // 04 · INTERACTION & DESIGN SYSTEM Tactile Calm: Warm Tones & Fluid Typography Vellum utilizes a muted stone palette, generous touch targets (minimum 48px), and gentle spring transitions. Check-ins are achieved with a single thumb swipe, and reflection prompts provide intelligent micro-suggestions based on current mood state. Fig 4.1 — Focused Freeform Journaling Mode Fig 4.2 — Longitudinal Emotional Clarity Trends // 05 · OUTCOMES & REFLECTION What the Design Delivers Vellum is published to the Figma Community with its full component library, so the typography, the low-pressure flow and the components can be inspected directly. 3 Modes Mood Check-In, Guided Breathing or Free Writing 0 Streaks No Streak Counters and No Red Badges Auto Layout Component Library on Auto Layout & Variables What I would test next: whether removing streaks and badges keeps people coming back as well as game-style loops do. That is the design's central bet, and it is untested. ← PREVIOUS CASE STUDY 05 · Lumina Analytics (Study & Focus Dashboard) NEXT CASE STUDY → 07 · FinTrack App (FinTech UX)
